reasoning: Both sets use the same machinery: a single package, a frozen-interface Phase 0, spine/thicken/wiring phases and a system task, with roadmap, plan and todo in agreement. B wins on content. Its RL design is stronger and closer to the brief. It builds a tabular → DQN → CNN ladder with ablations, a corridor that sanity-checks the shared core, and REINFORCE → PPO in a circular tank (as the brief says). It has one learning predator and an actual opponent-pool self-play rung with cross-play ratings, which is the 'co-evolution / self-play' concept the brief asks for. B's golden cases are concrete and arithmetically correct (TC-07, TC-12, TC-42 values, TC-52), and its noise-test bound is justified (≤3 of 20, p≈0.016). A changes the tank to a square, uses two predators, offers co-training without self-play, and sets a flaky oracle in TC-17 (≤1 of 20 rejections at family-wise α=0.05 fails about 26% of the time). A's M1 also gates every batch on an online one-step Q-learner solving the corridor. A has a cleaner milestone split and more Exit criteria, but its dependency graph is weaker. Spines write other owners' modules (DQN → methods/factory.py, train_loop → runlog/writer.py). The thicken tasks T28/T29 must hook into curve.py, which neither lists in Writes:. T17 leaves a private `verdict` stub in a file it doesn't own. B's weak spots are organisational. It keeps process narration in architecture.md ('adopted before M1 is built', 'TC-01–TC-49 don't change'), its brief is stale ('Not doing: Designing future environments now'), and its spines T09/T12 depend on unfrozen lab.build and lab.players functions. In both sets, packet buildability is the weakest area.
